quests.hint: Think about the season when the world starts turning green again.
quests.explanation: Great job! The season after winter, full of blooming flowers, is called spring.
quests.funFact: Many trees grow new leaves for the very first time each year during spring.
quests.wordExample: The garden was full of color in spring.

quests.hint: Think about the season with the most heat and the most daylight.
quests.explanation: Great job! The hottest, sunniest season with the longest days is called summer.
quests.funFact: Some places near the poles get sunshine almost all day long during summer.
quests.wordExample: We swam every day during summer.

quests.hint: Think of the season known for changeable mornings that start grey.
quests.explanation: Yes! Spring mornings often start cloudy before turning brighter later.
quests.funFact: Spring weather can change from cloudy to sunny in just a few hours.
quests.wordExample: Spring mornings often began cloudy before turning bright.

quests.hint: Think of the mild season between winter and summer.
quests.explanation: Correct! Soft rain showers that help flowers grow are common in spring.
quests.funFact: Spring rain adds water to the soil that helps new seeds sprout.
quests.wordExample: Spring showers helped the garden bloom.

quests.hint: Think of the season that makes people want to cool off in water.
quests.explanation: Correct! Beach trips, swimming, and ice cream are all common in summer.
quests.funFact: Ice cream sales usually rise the most during the hot summer months.
quests.wordExample: We ate ice cream at the beach during summer.

quests.hint: Think about the cooling water activity families enjoy on summer afternoons.
quests.explanation: Correct! Going swimming is an activity many families enjoy on summer afternoons.
quests.funFact: Lakes often feel cooler for swimming than the warm summer air outside.
quests.wordExample: We went swimming together during our summer afternoon at the lake.

quests.hint: Think about the season when many animal families welcome new babies.
quests.explanation: Yes! Many baby animals are born and nests are built during spring.
quests.funFact: Many birds return from warmer places to build nests in spring.
quests.wordExample: We saw baby animals during spring.

quests.hint: Think about the season when many children have their longest break from school.
quests.explanation: Yes! Many children have their longest school break during summer.
quests.funFact: Summer break gives many children extra time to play outside.
quests.wordExample: We had a long break from school during summer.

quests.hint: Think about the leg covering best suited for hot summer afternoons.
quests.explanation: Correct! Shorts help you stay comfortable during hot summer afternoons.
quests.funFact: Many families pack shorts for every warm summer outing.
quests.wordExample: I wore shorts during our hot summer afternoon at the pool.

quests.hint: Think about the season with weather that changes often, day to day.
quests.explanation: Correct! Weather that changes often between sun, clouds, and rain describes spring.
quests.funFact: Spring weather can shift from sunny to rainy in the very same day.
quests.wordExample: Spring weather changed quickly this week.

quests.hint: Think about the season with the most hours of daylight.
quests.explanation: Correct! Long days with a late sunset describe summer.
quests.funFact: The longest day of the whole year happens during summer.
quests.wordExample: The sun set late during a summer evening.

quests.hint: Think about the item that blocks spring rain showers on the walk to school.
quests.explanation: Correct! An umbrella helps you stay dry during spring showers.
quests.funFact: Spring's mix of sun and rain often means an umbrella is handy to carry.
quests.wordExample: I carried an umbrella during spring showers.

quests.hint: Think about the season when fields are prepared for new growing plants.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Farmers plant new seeds in their fields during spring.
quests.funFact: Spring soil is often just warm enough for seeds to begin sprouting.
quests.wordExample: Farmers planted seeds in their fields during spring.

quests.hint: Think about the season with heat strong enough to warm the sand.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Heat strong enough to warm beach sand describes summer.
quests.funFact: Deserts can get so hot in summer that sand becomes too warm to walk on barefoot.
quests.wordExample: The sand felt warm under our feet during summer.

quests.hint: Think of the season known for its warmest, sunniest days.
quests.explanation: Yes! Summer often brings the hottest days of the year.
quests.funFact: The hottest month of the year is often July or August in many countries.
quests.wordExample: Summer brought many hot days this year.

quests.hint: Think about the season that sits right in the middle, warming up slowly.
quests.explanation: Yes! The mild season between winter and summer is called spring.
quests.funFact: Daylight hours grow longer and longer as spring continues toward summer.
quests.wordExample: Spring is the season between winter and summer.

quests.hint: Think about the season that follows spring and brings the most heat.
quests.explanation: Yes! The season right after spring, bringing the most heat, is summer.
quests.funFact: Many fruits like watermelon and berries ripen during the summer months.
quests.wordExample: Summer followed spring with warm, sunny days.

quests.hint: Think of the season that gradually moves from warm to a bit chilly.
quests.explanation: Yes! Autumn days often become cool as the season continues.
quests.funFact: Autumn temperatures usually drop little by little from warm to cool.
quests.wordExample: Autumn days slowly turned cool here.

quests.hint: Think about the season famous for colorful blooming flowers.
quests.explanation: Correct! Tulips, daffodils, and cherry blossoms often bloom during spring.
quests.funFact: Cherry blossom trees can bloom for only a couple of weeks each spring.
quests.wordExample: Tulips bloomed brightly during spring.

quests.hint: Think about the season known for family vacations and outdoor picnics.
quests.explanation: Correct! Family vacations and outdoor picnics are common during summer.
quests.funFact: Many families plan road trips or vacations during the summer break.
quests.wordExample: We went on vacation during summer.

quests.hint: Think of the season known for gusty, changeable weather.
quests.explanation: Yes! Spring often brings gusty, windy days as the weather changes.
quests.funFact: Spring winds can help scatter seeds that grow into new spring flowers.
quests.wordExample: Spring brought many windy days this year.

quests.hint: Think about the season with chilly starts and warmer endings to each day.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Chilly mornings turning into warmer afternoons describe spring weather.
quests.funFact: Temperatures in spring can rise a great deal between morning and afternoon.
quests.wordExample: Chilly mornings warmed up by afternoon during spring.

quests.hint: Think about the season with hot days and evenings that stay bright late.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Hot afternoons with late, bright evenings describe summer.
quests.funFact: Warm summer evenings often stay light until quite late at night.
quests.wordExample: Warm evenings stayed bright late during summer.

quests.hint: Think of the season known for its chilliest, iciest days.
quests.explanation: Yes! Winter often brings the coldest days of the year.
quests.funFact: The coldest month of the year is often January in many countries.
quests.wordExample: Winter brought many cold days this year.

quests.hint: Think about the season when gardens get planted and cleaned up.
quests.explanation: Yes! Planting flowers and cleaning up gardens is a common spring activity.
quests.funFact: Spring cleaning is a tradition many families do around their homes and gardens.
quests.wordExample: We planted flowers and cleaned the garden during spring.

quests.hint: Think about the season when people dress to stay cool and protected from the sun.
quests.explanation: Yes! Shorts, sunglasses, and sunscreen help people stay comfortable during summer.
quests.funFact: Sunscreen helps protect skin from strong summer sunlight.
quests.wordExample: We wore sunglasses and shorts during summer.

quests.hint: Think about the head covering best suited for long, sunny summer afternoons.
quests.explanation: Correct! A sun hat helps protect you during long, sunny summer afternoons.
quests.funFact: Many families pack a sun hat for every member before a summer outing.
quests.wordExample: I wore a sun hat during our summer afternoon at the park.

quests.hint: Think about which season sits right after winter on the calendar.
quests.explanation: Correct! The season right after winter and before summer is spring.
quests.funFact: A full year has four seasons, and spring is usually the second one on many calendars.
quests.wordExample: Spring followed winter on the calendar.

quests.hint: Think about which season sits right after spring and before autumn.
quests.explanation: Correct! The season between spring and autumn is summer.
quests.funFact: A full year has four seasons, and summer is usually the warmest one.
quests.wordExample: Summer came between spring and autumn on the calendar.

quests.hint: Think of the season known for sudden afternoon weather changes.
quests.explanation: Correct! Summer afternoons can sometimes turn quickly into stormy weather.
quests.funFact: Summer storms often build up quickly on hot, humid afternoons.
quests.wordExample: Summer afternoons sometimes turned stormy here.
